bundles.evidenceText: this cause must be an uncaused change less time less and immaterial being which created the universe
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the universe began, has a transcendent cause, and that this cause must be uncaused, timeless, spaceless, and immaterial. That proposition directly supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge and cannot remain true without making that bridge more credible. The pro central bridge is excluded because the move establishes only the cosmological line, not the cumulative convergence of all five lines.

bundles.evidenceText: scientific beliefs do not depend on cultural indoctrination for their acceptance and transmission
bundles.rationale: The move contrasts scientific progress and critical scrutiny with the cultural and geographical transmission of religion. That proposition can remain true without making any stated bridge more or less credible, so it has no route contact and no applicable polarity. The nearest candidate, support for the con central bridge, is excluded because the excerpt does not specifically show that the five proposed evidential inferences are underdetermined or face contrary empirical evidence.

bundles.evidenceText: the world we see just doesn't match up to what you'd expect from a perfect God
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the observed world's evil is contrary to what a perfect God would lead us to expect. This directly supports the con subsidiary-3 bridge, and the proposition cannot remain true without making that bridge more credible. The con motion bridge is excluded because the expressed evidential reason exactly matches the narrower evil-and-divine-expectation bridge; the broader skeptical conclusion is downstream.

bundles.evidenceText: it may well be that only in a world suffused with natural evil as well as moral evil then the maximum number of people would freely come God
bundles.rationale: The move proposes that natural and moral evil may serve God's purpose of maximizing freely chosen relationship with him. This attacks the con subsidiary-3 inference that such evil is less expected from a morally perfect God, and the proposition cannot remain true without weakening that inference. Support for the pro central bridge is excluded because this is a specific defense against the evil-based bridge, not an argument for cumulative convergence of all five pro evidential lines.
